item.title: Tailevu Rugby celebrates Rewa win by giving back to Nakelo District School
item.description: The players and team officials took part in the clean-up following their Skipper Provincial Cup victory over their neighbours. Tailevu Rugby says the initiative was an opportunity to give back to Nakelo District School, which has supported the union for decades.
item.content:encoded:
The players and team officials took part in the clean-up following their Skipper Provincial Cup victory over their neighbours.

Tailevu Rugby says the initiative was an opportunity to give back to Nakelo District School, which has supported the union for decades.

The school has provided its grounds as one of Tailevu Rugby's home venues for the Skipper Cup and Marama Cup competitions.

The union says while victories on the field are important, it also has a responsibility to serve the communities that continue to support the team.

Ministry of Environment and Climate Change has also commended the players and officials for the initiative.

Minister for Environment Lynda Tabuya says the players have demonstrated that leadership extends beyond the rugby field.

Tabuya describes the initiative as civic pride in action, saying sporting teams can use their influence to serve communities and encourage people to care for their surroundings.

Meanwhile, the Fresh Choice Tailevu Rugby women's side also had plenty to celebrate after recording a dominant victory over Rewa in the Marama Championship.

Tailevu women's player Ana Sassen says their success came from having the strength and knowledge to not only play rugby, but to play smart rugby.

Sassen thanked God for the victory and also acknowledged those who continue to support the team.

Tailevu Rugby says its message remains that rugby is about more than winning games, and includes serving communities, supporting schools and building relationships that can last for generations.

item.title: Savea ruled out of final Test against Springboks
item.description: Inspirational New Zealand captain Ardie Savea will miss the All Blacks' final Test against South Africa after suffering a shoulder injury in this morning's 29-24 defeat to the Springboks. The 32-year-old was forced from the field nine minutes before half-time in a major blow to the All Blacks, who now trail 2-1 in the four-Test series.
item.content:encoded:
Inspirational New Zealand captain Ardie Savea will miss the All Blacks' final Test against South Africa after suffering a shoulder injury in this morning's 29-24 defeat to the Springboks.

The 32-year-old was forced from the field nine minutes before half-time in a major blow to the All Blacks, who now trail 2-1 in the four-Test series.

Savea had scored two tries before his injury, but his departure allowed South Africa to gain greater control as they went on to secure a bruising victory at Soccer City.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie confirmed after the match that Savea would not travel with the team to the United States for the fourth Test .

The fourth Test will be played in Baltimore, USA next Sunday, with the All Blacks needing a victory to level the series.

The All Blacks will now have to regroup without their captain as they look to force a series decider with victory in Baltimore.

item.title: All Blacks and Springboks set for crucial third Test tomorrow at 3.10am
item.description: The All Blacks and Springboks will meet at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg tomorrow morning for the third instalment of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, with the four-Test series locked at 1-1. The All Blacks have been the more attacking side in 2026, averaging 36 points and 5.4 tries per Test, compared with South Africa’s 32.7 points and 4.3 tries.
item.content:encoded:
The All Blacks and Springboks will meet at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg tomorrow morning for the third instalment of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, with the four-Test series locked at 1-1.

The All Blacks have been the more attacking side in 2026, averaging 36 points and 5.4 tries per Test, compared with South Africa’s 32.7 points and 4.3 tries.

New Zealand have also carried the ball more often and made almost 1,000 metres per match, while the Springboks have relied more heavily on their kicking game and set-piece strength.

The All Blacks’ tackle success rate of 87.7 percent is better than South Africa’s 83.6 percent, while the Springboks have the advantage at lineout time with a 93.9 percent success rate.

South Africa won the most recent encounter 33-26 in Cape Town last week, after the All Blacks opened the series with a 33-16 victory at Ellis Park.

Will Jordan has been a key attacking threat for New Zealand, scoring eight tries in five Tests, while Ardie Savea will again lead the side as captain.

For the Springboks, Cheslin Kolbe has been their leading points scorer with 44 points, while Jesse Kriel has scored four tries in five Tests.

With the series tied, tomorrow's clash at 3.10am is expected to be another closely fought encounter as both sides look to take control ahead of the fourth and final Test.

item.title: Springboks stage second-half comeback to edge All Blacks 29-24
item.description: South Africa staged a second-half comeback to defeat the All Blacks 29-24 at FNB Stadium in Johannesburgh, with Malcolm Marx and Jesse Kriel scoring crucial tries before Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s late penalty helped the Springboks hold off a dramatic New Zealand fightback. The victory gives the Springboks a 2-1 lead in the four-Test Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.
item.content:encoded:
South Africa staged a second-half comeback to defeat the All Blacks 29-24 at FNB Stadium in Johannesburgh, with Malcolm Marx and Jesse Kriel scoring crucial tries before Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s late penalty helped the Springboks hold off a dramatic New Zealand fightback.

The victory gives the Springboks a 2-1 lead in the four-Test Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

New Zealand made the stronger start, with captain Ardie Savea crossing for the opening try in the 10th minute before Ruben Love converted to give the All Blacks a 7-0 lead.

Kurt-Lee Arendse responded with South Africa’s opening try in the 20th minute, before Savea crossed for his second five minutes later as New Zealand moved 12-5 ahead.

However, the Springboks were awarded a penalty try in the 36th minute, bringing the scores level at 12-all heading into half-time.

The All Blacks regained the lead in the 55th minute when Will Jordan crossed to make it 17-12, but the advantage did not last long.

Jesse Kriel hit back with a try two minutes later and Feinberg-Mngomezulu converted as South Africa took the lead for the first time at 19-17.

The momentum then swung firmly towards the Springboks, with replacement hooker Malcolm Marx powering over in the 65th minute.

Feinberg-Mngomezulu added the conversion to stretch South Africa’s advantage to 26-17 before landing a penalty in the 70th minute to give the hosts a 12-point cushion at 29-17.

The All Blacks refused to go away and launched one final attack, with Samisoni Taukei'aho scoring after the 80-minute mark and Damian McKenzie converting.

But the late seven-pointer was not enough, as South Africa held on for the 29-24 victory in Johannesburg.

Both sides finished with four tries, but South Africa’s second-half surge and Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s boot ultimately proved the difference.

The two rugby heavyweights will now head to Baltimore in the United States for the fourth and final Test next Sunday, with kick-off at 9am.

item.title: Tailevu U20 snatch late win over Rewa 21-20 in Skipper Cup
item.description: Tailevu U20 staged a dramatic late comeback to edge FMF Rewa 21-20, with Itu Josaia scoring a crucial try in the dying minutes before Saiyasi Nayacalevu converted to seal the victory. Rewa had mounted a strong second-half comeback and were leading Tailevu by six points late in the match.
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu U20 staged a dramatic late comeback to edge FMF Rewa 21-20, with Itu Josaia scoring a crucial try in the dying minutes before Saiyasi Nayacalevu converted to seal the victory.

Rewa had mounted a strong second-half comeback and were leading Tailevu by six points late in the match.

With time running out, Josaia crossed for Tailevu to bring them within one point of Rewa.

Nayacalevu then stepped up and successfully converted the try to put Tailevu ahead and secure the narrow victory.

Tailevu acknowledged Rewa for providing a tough contest and wished them well for their upcoming matches.

Meanwhile, the Tailevu women's side produced a dominant performance against their neighbours, defeating Rewa 102-0.

Despite challenging ground conditions, the Tailevu women successfully executed their game plan and kept Rewa scoreless throughout the match.

In other Marama Championship results, Namosi thrashed Lautoka 91-7, Nadroga defeated Ba 51-42, Taveuni edged Naitasiri 22-19, Nadi beat Nasinu 32-31, while Suva defeated Kadavu 19-10.

In the Skipper Provincial Cup Under-20 competition, Suva beat Kadavu 26-3, Naitasiri defeated Taveuni 13-0, Nadroga beat Ba 20-15, Nadi defeated Navosa 41-5, while Malolo recorded a convincing 52-21 victory over Lautoka.

In the senior competition, Malolo edged Lautoka 29-25, Nadroga beat Ba 56-24, Namosi defeated Rewa 32-15, Naitasiri beat Taveuni 25-18, Suva defeated Kadavu 25-8, while Nadi recorded a 31-12 victory over Navosa.
